newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG RETURN TO PARC ON HIGH NOTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG RETURN TO PARC ON HIGH NOTE.

text.p: Paris St Germain, their standing as a top European side restored with a fine Cup Winners' Cup victory in Athens, plunge back into the French league title race with renewed confidence and hope at home to Metz on Sunday.
PSG travelled to Athens for Thursday's quarter-final second leg against AEK Athens at a low ebb after a 1-0 league defeat at lowly Le Havre last weekend, one more black spot in a calamitous season.

Now the holders, drawn against Liverpool in the semifinals and only the third club with Real Madrid and Ajax Amsterdam to reach that stage in European competition in five successive seasons, believe they can turn the domestic tide too.

The club's Brazilian captain Rai said: "This is the same PSG with a different morale and greater solidarity. We feel good together and now we're going to be more regular. The hardest part is behind us.

"We feel we're playing better and that's the biggest satisfaction," added Rai, who had a superb game at the hub of the PSG midfield, after a Patrice Loko hat-trick had put them through after being held 0-0 by AEK in the home leg.
"After the 1-0 defeat at Le Havre in the championship we told ourselves that it was an accident and we should quickly forget it."
The loss came after their first home win in more than four months, 3-1 against Lyon the previous weekend, which was seen as a turning point.
PSG executive president Michel Denisot said: "We are also fighting in the championship but it will be difficult because Monaco have a great team perfectly capabale of a league and UEFA Cup double."
Monaco, seven clear at the top of the first division with nine games to go, will be hard to catch but PSG can still qualify for the European Cup next season by finishing second.

Monaco are at home to fifth-placed Bastia, one of a group of teams vying with PSG for the second European Cup berth, on Saturday. Of the others, Strasbourg, Bordeaux and Nantes are best placed, with defending champions Auxerre and Metz close behind.
